reviewer.independence: Did not implement commit 6caa3d93 or candidate commit 178883656d401630b88fadfc603a45af3f27da50, worked only in the isolated worktree, and edited only held-out perturbation artifacts plus this review record.

prior_reviews.note: The prior review rejected the first implementation because package URLs were still dropped from the Rust model. The exact candidate fixes that carry-through gap, but the held-out follow-up matrix below still rejects it on separate Java-behavior mismatches.

java: CommandPackage and CommandPackageWithUSymbol accept tags, stereotype, URL, and trailing color after the package code/display. On reopen they mutate stereotype only when the current declaration supplies one, so an earlier stereotype survives a plain `package systems.api { ... }` reopen.

UrlBuilder returns Url objects with relative href resolution via `topurl`; SVG link serialization then happens through `UGraphicSvg.startUrl` and `SvgGraphics.LinkData`, which applies `SkinParam.getSvgLinkTarget()` and normalizes tooltip text by decoding `<U+XXXX>` escapes and replacing literal `\n` with a newline.
rust: ClassParser::try_package now carries URL metadata into Package, but when it reuses an existing final package it unconditionally assigns `package.stereotypes = stereotypes.clone()`. A reopen without a stereotype therefore clears the original stereotype instead of preserving it.
emit_package_link_open serializes `tooltip.unwrap_or(href)` literally. It does not reproduce Java's `SvgGraphics.LinkData.getXlinkTitle()` decoding of `<U+XXXX>` sequences or literal `\n`.

The product renderer loses `skinparam svgLinkTarget` because parser-side metadata canonicalization lowercases keys to `svglinktarget`, while `skinparam::apply_skinparams` only lowercases the first character and matches the camel-case string `svgLinkTarget`.

perturbations.evidence: Java keeps the outer package stereotype `<<Facade>>` from the first declaration when `package systems.api { ... }` reopens it later. The exact candidate clears that stereotype on reopen, removing the stereotype line, shrinking `systems.api` from 231px to 215px and its parent `systems` from 255px to 239px, and moving both child entities up by 16px.

Java emits target `_blank` and title `Docs & Support` for the package anchor. The exact candidate emits target `_top` and the literal undecoded title `Docs <U+0026> Support` even though the href is correctly resolved to `https://docs.example/root/runtime/index.html`.

Java's anchor title is the two-line string `Docs\nPortal` normalized to an actual newline in SVG. The exact candidate serializes the literal backslash sequence, producing `Docs\\nPortal` in both `title` and `xlink:title`.

Java emits `href=""`, target `_parent`, and title `Tooltip & More`. The exact candidate emits the same empty href but falls back to target `_top` and leaves the tooltip undecoded as `Tooltip <U+0026> More`.

findings: Reject: the exact candidate still does not match Java package URL behavior on held-out valid inputs.
Reopening an existing package without re-stating its stereotype clears the stored stereotype in Rust, while Java preserves it. This changes cluster header content and layout geometry.
Package anchor titles are serialized too literally in Rust. Java decodes `<U+XXXX>` sequences and literal `\n` before writing `title` and `xlink:title`; the exact candidate does not.

Product `skinparam svgLinkTarget` is ineffective for package links on the no-oracle path because parser-side lowercasing (`svglinktarget`) does not match the renderer's camel-case `svgLinkTarget` switch arm, so Rust falls back to `_top`.
